transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what finally pushed me to call the employee assistance program was my sleep. I’m just barely sleeping right lately. I’ll lie there for hours replaying stuff from work, or arguments at home, and then I wake up at like 3 or 4 in the morning and my brain just starts again.

It’s weird because I used to be the guy who could sleep anywhere — hotel rooms, airports, after sales conferences, all that. But now I start the day feeling like I never really rested, and then I’m just dragging. So… yeah, that’s what brought me in.

When you’re lying awake or waking up in the middle of the night, how are you feeling emotionally — are these times when you feel particularly down, hopeless, or unable to enjoy anything, or more just stressed and overwhelmed?

Yeah… it’s not just stress, I don’t think. I mean, work stuff kicks it off sometimes, but even when there’s nothing specific going on, I’ve got this… heavy, gray kind of mood that just follows me around. Like from the office to the car and then into the house.

I’ll be sitting there and everyone’s doing normal evening stuff, and I’m thinking about emails I forgot to send, or whether the Q4 numbers are going to be a mess — sorry, that’s not really what you asked. It’s more like I feel hollow a lot of days. Not crying or anything dramatic, just… flat and weighed down.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Yeah… I have noticed that. Like, I used to really look forward to pickup basketball with some guys from work, or bowling nights, or going to music festivals when we could get tickets. And I used to love firing up the smoker and having people over — I’d make way too much brisket, everyone would hang out in the yard, that kind of thing.

Lately, though, I either cancel because it feels like too much effort, or I go and I’m just… there. Like I’m saying the right things and laughing at the right moments, but it doesn’t really land. I feel like I’m going through the motions more than actually enjoying it.
Have you had times when you've felt like you're a failure or that you'd be better off dead?

Yeah… I mean, failure, yeah, that word hits a little too close. I’ll think about stuff I dropped at work or times I’m not really present at home, and it just turns into this whole mental spreadsheet of everything I’m not doing right.

And, um… I should say, I’m not making some plan to hurt myself. I don’t have, like, a plan. But the thought does come up more than I want to admit that maybe everyone would be better off if I just… didn’t wake up one morning. Then I feel guilty even thinking that, because I know that’s a horrible thing to put on people, and then I start thinking about how I’ve got a meeting the next day or the lawn still needs mowing, which sounds stupid, but… yeah. It’s there sometimes.
Over the last two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, or have you experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in most activities nearly every day?

Yeah… most days, honestly. It’s like this heavy, gray mood kind of follows me around — from the office to the car, then home — and it’s not always tied to something specific. Like, I’ll be thinking maybe it’s just a bad sales call or some random thing with the team, but even on quieter days it’s still there. I just feel kind of hollow a lot of the time.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently — like eating a lot more or a lot less than usual?

Yeah, it’s been… kind of all over the place, I guess. My appetite’s been off for months. I’ll get to work and just run on coffee, and then suddenly it’s like 2 p.m. and I never ate lunch. Which, honestly, I used to be the guy reminding everyone to grab food between calls.

Dinner’s weird too. I’ll sit with my family and kind of pick at whatever’s there, and then I’ll realize I barely touched it. But then somehow my belt is sitting a notch tighter than it used to, so I don’t know — maybe I’m eating random stuff later or just not paying attention. I had to change notches the other day and it annoyed me more than it should’ve.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?

Yeah… a little. I don’t think anyone at work would be like, “Wow, he’s really falling apart,” or anything. I’m still showing up, still in meetings, still doing the sales manager act, you know.

But I notice it. I’ll sit there staring at my laptop way longer than makes sense, like I’m about to answer an email and then five minutes go by and I’m still just… looking at it. And sometimes one of my reps asks me something simple, like about a client follow-up, and I know the answer, but there’s this extra beat before I respond. It’s embarrassing.

I don’t know if I’d call it restless exactly. More like everything takes a little more effort to get moving.
Over the last two weeks, have you felt a noticeable drop in your energy level or felt fatigued even without much activity, nearly every day?

I don’t know… energy is hard to pin down. I mean, I feel worn out sometimes, but who doesn’t, right? Sales is kind of a grind — there’s always some number someone’s asking about, and half the day is just putting out little fires.

But like… nearly every day? I’m not sure I’d say that. I haven’t really been tracking it. Some days I get through the day okay, and other days I’m just kind of dragging. Then again, I’ll blame it on sleep or work or too much coffee, which probably isn’t helpful. So… I guess I’ve noticed it here and there, but I’m not sure if it’s a big noticeable drop.
Have you found that you no longer take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even when you're not particularly tired or stressed?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I used to really look forward to stuff — like pickup basketball, bowling nights with the guys, music festivals when we could get tickets, even just firing up the smoker and having people over. I was kind of annoying about the smoker, honestly… always talking about rubs and wood chips and whether brisket was worth getting up at 5 a.m. for.

Lately, though, I either cancel or I go and it’s like I’m there but not really in it. Basketball feels like something on the calendar instead of something I want to do. Bowling, I’ll show up and make small talk, but I’m mostly waiting until it’s okay to leave. Even cooking for friends just feels like a project.

So yeah, even when I’m not completely wiped out or slammed at work, it’s like the fun part doesn’t really land the same.
Can you think of a time recently when you genuinely enjoyed something, even a small thing, and looked forward to it beforehand?

Honestly… I’m trying to think of one. Maybe there’ve been little moments, but nothing I really looked forward to the way I used to.

Like, I used to get kind of excited about pickup basketball or bowling night, or if there was a music festival coming up I’d be checking the lineup and texting people about it. And the smoker thing — I used to make this whole production out of having people over, like I was running some backyard barbecue joint.

Lately it’s more like… I either cancel, or I go and I’m just kind of doing the steps. I’m there, I’m talking, I’m smiling when I’m supposed to. But I’m mostly thinking about when I can leave. So, yeah, I’m not sure I’ve had that “looking forward to it” feeling much recently.
Would you say that you’ve lost pleasure in almost all activities, to the point where very few things — even ones you used to enjoy — feel rewarding or satisfying anymore?

Yeah… I mean, “almost all” sounds big, but… it does feel like most of the stuff that used to actually do something for me doesn’t anymore.

Like I said, pickup basketball used to be the thing I’d arrange my week around, and bowling nights were dumb but fun, you know? Half the time we weren’t even bowling well, just talking trash. And music festivals — I used to get way too into the lineup. Or having people over and using the smoker… I’d spend all day messing with it, checking temperatures like I was on some cooking show.

Lately I either don’t go, or I go and it’s like I’m just… completing the activity. Showing up, making conversation, leaving when I can. It doesn’t really feel rewarding the way it used to. So yeah, I guess very few things feel satisfying lately.

The patient reported persistent low mood, loss of interest in previously enjoyable activities, and emotional flatness, which supports the continuation of F33.1 (Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode moderate) and F51.03 (Insomnia disorder with non-somatic symptoms). F43.22 (Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood) is ruled out due to the persistence and severity of symptoms beyond a typical adjustment reaction. G47.00 (Insomnia, unspecified) is also ruled out as the insomnia is better characterized within the context of a mood disorder.

The patient endorsed persistent feelings of failure, anhedonia, emotional flatness, and passive suicidal ideation without a plan. These symptoms continue to align with both F33.1 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder, current episode moderate) and F51.03 (Insomnia disorder with associated mental disorder). No new information sufficiently narrows the differential further at this point.

The patient continues to endorse key symptoms of depression, including persistent low mood, anhedonia, sleep disturbance, feelings of worthlessness, and passive suicidal ideation. These symptoms are consistent with both recurrent major depressive disorder (F33.1) and major depressive disorder, unspecified (F51.03). No new information has been provided to rule out either diagnosis definitively.
